title: fix: handle snippy post-insertion rejection to avoid unhandled error (fixes #331807)
body:
### Summary The Copilot code-referencing ("snippy") post-insertion check is fired as an unawaited, uncaught floating promise from `NextEditProvider.runSnippy`. When the snippy service returns a non-200 response, `SnippyFetchService.fetch` throws, `handlePostInsertion` re-throws, and — because the promise is neither awaited nor given a rejection handler — the error surfaces as an unhandled rejection that is reported to error telemetry. The specific 400 seen here (`source too short (must be at least 110 tokens, but is 105)`) is an expected server-side rejection: the client's local pre-check uses a 65-lexeme minimum while the service enforces its own, higher token minimum, so short accepted suggestions routinely trip it. Impact is noisy telemetry only — no user-facing functionality breaks. Fixes microsoft/vscode#331807 Recommended reviewer: `@ulugbekna` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | `333d9a4053e` (vendored-import boundary) | | Author | `@not-determined` | | PR | n/a | | Message | Initial import of the Copilot Chat extension ("Hello Copilot") | | Why | The fire-and-forget `handlePostInsertion(...)` call in `runSnippy` has existed without a rejection handler since the extension was vendored into `microsoft/vscode`. `git blame` shows the throwing call site predates all recent changes, so this is a **pre-existing** bug re-bucketed by telemetry (the specific 400 message text changed the bucket), not a new regression. | > Pre-existing / re-bucketing: the underlying floating-promise pattern is not introduced by any recent commit in the regression window; the new bucket is driven by the server's error-message text, not by a change in triggering logic. ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant User as User accepts NES participant NEP as NextEditProvider.runSnippy participant Svc as SnippyService.handlePostInsertion participant Fetch as SnippyFetchService.fetch participant Server as Snippy service User->>NEP: handleAcceptance() Note over NEP: ⚠️ Root cause:
handlePostInsertion() called
without await / .catch NEP->>Svc: handlePostInsertion(uri, doc, edit) Svc->>Fetch: fetchMatch(source) Fetch->>Server: POST snippy/match Server-->>Fetch: 400 "source too short (110 > 105)" Note over Fetch: 💥 throw new Error(`Failed with status 400 ...`) Fetch-->>Svc: rejects Svc-->>NEP: rejects (floating promise) Note over NEP: Unhandled rejection → error telemetry ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `extensions/copilot/src/extension/inlineEdits/node/nextEditProvider.ts` | root cause / fix site | L1648-1653: `this._snippyService.handlePostInsertion(...)` called with no `await` and no `.catch`, so a rejection escapes as an unhandled error | | `extensions/copilot/src/platform/snippy/common/snippyServiceImpl.ts` | rethrow site | L40-44: `catch (e) { throw e; }` re-throws the fetch failure up to the floating caller | | `extensions/copilot/src/platform/snippy/common/snippyFetcher.ts` | crash site | L70-71: `if (fetchResponse.status !== 200) { throw new Error(\`Failed with status \$\{status} ...\`); }` | | `extensions/copilot/src/platform/snippy/common/snippyCompute.ts` | contributing mismatch | L8: `MinTokenLength = 65` — client pre-check floor is looser than the service's 110-token floor, so short sources pass the client gate but are rejected by the server | ### Repro Steps 1. Use the Copilot Chat extension with Next Edit Suggestions (code referencing / public-code matching enabled). 2. Accept a short next-edit suggestion whose surrounding source clears the client's local 65-lexeme pre-check but is below the snippy service's token minimum (~110 tokens). 3. `runSnippy` fires `handlePostInsertion`; the snippy `/match` request returns HTTP 400 (`source too short`). 4. Because the promise is unawaited and uncaught, the rejection surfaces as an unhandled error and is reported to telemetry. Deterministic given a source between the two thresholds; otherwise triggered whenever the service rejects the request for any reason. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** (`nextEditProvider.ts`): `runSnippy` now `await`s `handlePostInsertion(...)` inside a `try/catch` and routes any failure to `this._logService.error(e, ...)`. This attaches a rejection handler at the fire-and-forget boundary that owns the background operation, so the failure is recorded as a *handled* error through the existing log/telemetry pipeline instead of escaping as an unhandled rejection. This follows the principle of fixing the error at the boundary that owns the best-effort background work — snippy code-referencing is explicitly a best-effort check, so its failures should not appear as unhandled application errors. The `logService.error` call preserves telemetry visibility of genuine failures; nothing is silently swallowed. **Alternatives considered:** - Aligning the client `MinTokenLength` (65) with the server's 110-token floor — rejected: the exact server threshold is not a stable contract the client can safely hardcode, other non-200 responses would still leak, and it would not fix the underlying missing-rejection-handler defect. - Swallowing the error inside `snippyServiceImpl.handlePostInsertion` (removing the rethrow) — rejected: that hides all fetch failures from callers/telemetry rather than handling them at the fire-and-forget site, and would violate the "never silence errors" principle by dropping them entirely. ### Recommended Owner `@ulugbekna` — dominant recent author of `nextEditProvider.ts` (author of the most recent NES/inline-edits commits touching this file, merged into `microsoft/vscode`), making them the natural owner for this fire-and-forget call site in the inline-edits area. > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/32384235362) · opus48 · 461.5 AIC · ⌖ 11.7 AIC · ⊞ 18.6K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests)

title: Fix server error retry logic to prevent over-retries
body:
This pull request addresses the issue of server responses that are errors (non-2xx) incorrectly triggering the network stack fallback logic, leading to excessive retries. The changes made include:

- **Updated `fetcherFallback.ts`**: Modified the logic to return any non-2xx response immediately, preventing fallback or health changes from being triggered.
- **Enhanced `fetcherFallback.spec.ts`**: Added tests for 401, 429, and 503 responses across the Electron, Node fetch, and Node HTTPS stacks to ensure that only the active fetcher is called and the original response is preserved.
- **Maintained fallback behavior**: Ensured that fallback logic remains intact for transport exceptions and malformed JSON on successful responses.

Validation was performed using the targeted Vitest suite, which passed successfully, confirming that the implementation works as intended.

title: Agent Host session restore is canceled by no-op proxy configuration restart
body:
## Summary

After quitting and restarting VS Code Insiders, the previously open Agents Window session can display a persistent:

> Couldn't open session
>
> Canceled

The session still exists and is healthy. A retry moments later restores the same session with its complete history, but the initial transient failure has already been rendered into the chat model and remains visible.

## Specific user impact

On every affected restart, the user's previously active agent session appears unrecoverable even though no session data was lost. The restored editor is left on a blocking error instead of the conversation, so the user cannot immediately continue where they left off and may reasonably believe that the session and its work have been lost. Recovery depends on triggering another subscription, such as navigating away from the session and back, rather than happening automatically.

## Reproduction

1. Open an existing Copilot Agent Host session in the Agents Window.
2. Quit VS Code.
3. Start VS Code and allow the previous window/session state to restore.
4. Observe that the restored session can show `Couldn't open session / Canceled`.
5. Navigate away and back, or otherwise cause a fresh subscription.
6. The same session loads successfully with its prior turns.

## Correlated timeline

From an Agent Host debug bundle captured on 2026-08-20:

- `08:23:27.947`: the window subscribes to the restored session, its default chat, and annotations.
- `08:23:27.948`: startup configuration synchronization sends the proxy settings. Both `http.proxy` and `http.proxyKerberosServicePrincipal` are empty strings.
- `08:23:29.137`: the initial Copilot client starts successfully.
- `08:23:31.842`: Agent Host logs `Restarting CopilotClient (CAPI proxy configuration changed ((none) -> (none)))`.
- `08:23:33.320`: Copilot chat discovery completes successfully: 4,294 SDK sessions were enumerated and the affected session was already known to Agent Host.
- `08:23:34.244`: resuming the affected chat backing fails with `Canceled`.
- `08:23:34.245`–`08:23:34.294`: the session, chat, and annotations subscriptions fail with JSON-RPC `-32603`: `Failed to restore session ...: Canceled`.
- `08:23:34.259`: the client issues another session subscription.
- `08:23:35.481`: the replacement Copilot client starts successfully.
- `08:23:38.905`: the same chat backing resumes successfully.
- `08:23:41.477`: Agent Host restores the same session with all 27 turns.
- `08:23:41.480`: the retry subscription succeeds.

This confirms that the session is present and restorable. Its initial restore is canceled while the Copilot client is restarted.

## Likely root cause

The initial Copilot client records an absent Kerberos proxy SPN as `undefined`. The synchronized default for `http.proxyKerberosServicePrincipal` is later received as `""`. In `CopilotAgent._refreshProxy()`, the strict comparison treats those two equivalent "no value" states as different:

```ts
const effectiveKerberosSpn = process.env['COPILOT_PROXY_KERBEROS_SPN'] || this._configurationService.getRootValue(...);
if (effectiveProxy === this._appliedProxy && effectiveKerberosSpn === this._appliedProxyKerberosSpn) {
	return;
}
```

The resulting restart is logged as `(none) -> (none)` because the message only includes the proxy URL, not the SPN difference. `_applyPendingClientRestart()` then clears the live SDK chat entries and stops the client while restoration is in progress, causing the resume operation to reject with `Canceled`.

The proxy-setting synchronization and Kerberos-SPN restart comparison were introduced in [#331488](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/331488).

## Relationship to #331648

This is related to [#331648](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/331648) in user-visible behavior, but it is a different host-side race:

- #331648 produced `AHP_SESSION_NOT_FOUND` because restore raced provider catalog migration.
- This occurrence produces JSON-RPC `-32603 / Canceled` after catalog discovery succeeds, because a no-op proxy configuration difference restarts the Copilot client during restore.
- The affected Insiders build already contains the fixes from [#331716](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/331716) and [#331721](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/331721).

Both failures become sticky because the workbench converts the first transient subscription failure into synthetic `Couldn't open session` chat history, even when a later subscription succeeds.

## Suggested fix

- Normalize empty proxy and Kerberos-SPN strings to `undefined` before storing and comparing effective values.
- Add a regression test proving that startup synchronization from an unset SPN to `""` does not restart the Copilot client.
- Consider making restoration resilient to unavoidable client restarts by delaying the restart while session restoration is active or retrying transient `Canceled` restore failures before rendering a permanent load error.

(Written by Copilot)

title: fix: handle snippy post-insertion rejection to avoid unhandled error (fixes #331807)
body:
### Summary The Copilot code-referencing ("snippy") post-insertion check is fired as an unawaited, uncaught floating promise from `NextEditProvider.runSnippy`. When the snippy service returns a non-200 response, `SnippyFetchService.fetch` throws, `handlePostInsertion` re-throws, and — because the promise is neither awaited nor given a rejection handler — the error surfaces as an unhandled rejection that is reported to error telemetry. The specific 400 seen here (`source too short (must be at least 110 tokens, but is 105)`) is an expected server-side rejection: the client's local pre-check uses a 65-lexeme minimum while the service enforces its own, higher token minimum, so short accepted suggestions routinely trip it. Impact is noisy telemetry only — no user-facing functionality breaks. Fixes microsoft/vscode\#331807 Recommended reviewer: `@ulugbekna` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | `333d9a4053e` (vendored-import boundary) | | Author | `@not-determined` | | PR | n/a | | Message | Initial import of the Copilot Chat extension ("Hello Copilot") | | Why | The fire-and-forget `handlePostInsertion(...)` call in `runSnippy` has existed without a rejection handler since the extension was vendored into `microsoft/vscode`. `git blame` shows the throwing call site predates all recent changes, so this is a **pre-existing** bug re-bucketed by telemetry (the specific 400 message text changed the bucket), not a new regression. | > Pre-existing / re-bucketing: the underlying floating-promise pattern is not introduced by any recent commit in the regression window; the new bucket is driven by the server's error-message text, not by a change in triggering logic. ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant User as User accepts NES participant NEP as NextEditProvider.runSnippy participant Svc as SnippyService.handlePostInsertion participant Fetch as SnippyFetchService.fetch participant Server as Snippy service User->>NEP: handleAcceptance() Note over NEP: ⚠️ Root cause:
handlePostInsertion() called
without await / .catch NEP->>Svc: handlePostInsertion(uri, doc, edit) Svc->>Fetch: fetchMatch(source) Fetch->>Server: POST snippy/match Server-->>Fetch: 400 "source too short (110 > 105)" Note over Fetch: 💥 throw new Error(`Failed with status 400 ...`) Fetch-->>Svc: rejects Svc-->>NEP: rejects (floating promise) Note over NEP: Unhandled rejection → error telemetry ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `extensions/copilot/src/extension/inlineEdits/node/nextEditProvider.ts` | root cause / fix site | L1648-1653: `this._snippyService.handlePostInsertion(...)` called with no `await` and no `.catch`, so a rejection escapes as an unhandled error | | `extensions/copilot/src/platform/snippy/common/snippyServiceImpl.ts` | rethrow site | L40-44: `catch (e) { throw e; }` re-throws the fetch failure up to the floating caller | | `extensions/copilot/src/platform/snippy/common/snippyFetcher.ts` | crash site | L70-71: `if (fetchResponse.status !== 200) { throw new Error(\`Failed with status \$\{status} ...\`); }` | | `extensions/copilot/src/platform/snippy/common/snippyCompute.ts` | contributing mismatch | L8: `MinTokenLength = 65` — client pre-check floor is looser than the service's 110-token floor, so short sources pass the client gate but are rejected by the server | ### Repro Steps 1. Use the Copilot Chat extension with Next Edit Suggestions (code referencing / public-code matching enabled). 2. Accept a short next-edit suggestion whose surrounding source clears the client's local 65-lexeme pre-check but is below the snippy service's token minimum (~110 tokens). 3. `runSnippy` fires `handlePostInsertion`; the snippy `/match` request returns HTTP 400 (`source too short`). 4. Because the promise is unawaited and uncaught, the rejection surfaces as an unhandled error and is reported to telemetry. Deterministic given a source between the two thresholds; otherwise triggered whenever the service rejects the request for any reason. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** (`nextEditProvider.ts`): `runSnippy` now `await`s `handlePostInsertion(...)` inside a `try/catch` and routes any failure to `this._logService.error(e, ...)`. This attaches a rejection handler at the fire-and-forget boundary that owns the background operation, so the failure is recorded as a *handled* error through the existing log/telemetry pipeline instead of escaping as an unhandled rejection. This follows the principle of fixing the error at the boundary that owns the best-effort background work — snippy code-referencing is explicitly a best-effort check, so its failures should not appear as unhandled application errors. The `logService.error` call preserves telemetry visibility of genuine failures; nothing is silently swallowed. **Alternatives considered:** - Aligning the client `MinTokenLength` (65) with the server's 110-token floor — rejected: the exact server threshold is not a stable contract the client can safely hardcode, other non-200 responses would still leak, and it would not fix the underlying missing-rejection-handler defect. - Swallowing the error inside `snippyServiceImpl.handlePostInsertion` (removing the rethrow) — rejected: that hides all fetch failures from callers/telemetry rather than handling them at the fire-and-forget site, and would violate the "never silence errors" principle by dropping them entirely. ### Recommended Owner `@ulugbekna` — dominant recent author of `nextEditProvider.ts` (author of the most recent NES/inline-edits commits touching this file, merged into `microsoft/vscode`), making them the natural owner for this fire-and-forget call site in the inline-edits area. > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/32384235362) · opus48 · 461.5 AIC · ⌖ 11.7 AIC · ⊞ 18.6K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests) --- > [!NOTE] > This was originally intended as a pull request, but PR creation failed. title: Remote AHP host custom agent is unavailable at session creation and cannot remain selected
body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Bundled with VS Code 1.134 client; remote Copilot CLI runtime 1.0.79-6
- VS Code Version: 1.134 client; remote standalone Agent Host 1.133.0 Stable (`a5b500951314efd502d07465bd138dfbd714a960`)
- OS Version: macOS 26 on Apple Silicon (client); Windows 11 (remote host)
- Feature: Agents window connected to a remote standalone Agent Host over an AHP tunnel
- Selected model: GPT-5.6 Sol, xhigh
- AHP version: 0.8

## Description

A user-level custom agent installed on a remote AHP host (`~/.copilot/agents/*.agent.md`) is discovered by the host and works when selected directly through AHP, but the VS Code Agents window cannot use it correctly.

This is specific to a custom agent supplied by a remote AHP host, not a workspace custom agent disappearing after the first prompt.

There are three related symptoms:

1. **The host custom agent is missing when creating a session.** In the new-session UI for the AHP tunnel, the Agent picker does not list the custom agent, so the session cannot be started with it.
2. **It appears after the session starts, but cannot be selected.** Once a default Copilot session exists, the custom agent appears under the Agent button. Clicking it does not change the active selection; the button remains on the default `Agent`.
3. **A direct AHP selection works for one turn, but the UI does not retain it.** Sending `chat/turnStarted` with the discovered custom agent's `message.agent.uri` runs that turn with the custom agent. After the turn completes and the session is viewed or continued in VS Code, the UI does not stay on that custom agent. The next UI-submitted message runs as the default assistant.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a standalone Agent Host on a remote machine and connect VS Code to it through an AHP tunnel.
2. Put a valid user-level custom agent on the host under `~/.copilot/agents/<name>.agent.md`.
3. In the macOS VS Code Agents window, start creating a new session on that AHP host.
4. Open the Agent picker.
5. Observe that the host custom agent is not available before session creation.
6. Start the session with the default Copilot agent.
7. Open the Agent picker in the running session.
8. Observe that the host custom agent is now listed.
9. Click the custom agent.
10. Observe that the active selection remains `Agent`; submitting a message uses the default assistant.
11. As a control, create/subscribe to a session over AHP and send the first `chat/turnStarted` with `message.agent.uri` set to the URI advertised for the host custom agent.
12. Observe that this turn correctly uses the custom agent.
13. Continue the same session from the VS Code Agents window.
14. Observe that the custom-agent selection is not retained and the next turn uses the default assistant.

## Diagnostic evidence

The host advertises the custom agent in the materialized session's `customizations`, with a file URI under the remote host's `~/.copilot/agents` directory. Direct AHP invocation using that URI succeeds, proving that the file is valid, discovered, and usable by the provider.

For the direct-AHP turn, the session records a successful custom-agent selection and follows its instructions. Before the next message submitted through the VS Code UI, the session records the equivalent of:

```text
custom agent selected
custom agent deselected
user message submitted
response uses default assistant
```

The selected model remains unchanged, and no selection error is shown to the user.

## Expected behavior

- Host-scoped custom agents should be available in the Agent picker while creating a session on that AHP host.
- Clicking a host custom agent in a running session should update the active Agent selection.
- After a custom agent is selected, the Agents window should retain that choice for subsequent messages (and after reopening the session) until the user explicitly selects another agent.
- UI-submitted turns should include the selected custom agent's `message.agent.uri`.

## Actual behavior

- The host custom agent is absent during new-session creation.
- It becomes visible only after a default session exists.
- Clicking it does not activate it.
- A direct AHP-selected custom agent works for one turn, but VS Code clears/omits the selection on the next UI turn without warning.

title: Feature request: invoke multiple Agent Skills from any position in Copilot Chat messages
body:
## Feature request: inline and multiple Agent Skill invocation

### Problem

Copilot Chat recognizes an Agent Skill slash command when `/` starts a message, but a slash reference typed after existing text is treated as ordinary text. This also prevents invoking multiple skills in one request.

### Reproduction

1. Open Copilot Chat or the Agents window.
2. Ensure an Agent Skill such as `code-review` and `test-runner` is available.
3. Type text first, then type `/` in the same message, for example:

```text
Review this change with /code-review and validate it with /test-runner.
```

4. Try to select both skills from autocomplete and submit the message.

### Actual behavior

Skill autocomplete/invocation is available when `/` starts the message, but inline slash references after existing text are treated as plain text. Multiple skills cannot be selected in one message.

### Expected behavior

- Typing `/` anywhere in the composer opens skill and prompt-file autocomplete.
- Multiple skills can be selected in one message.
- Selected skills are represented as structured references or chips.
- Existing leading slash-command behavior continues to work.

### Environment

- VS Code: `1.134.0` (`110a328ea54b42367b803ec53ee0bf52ef26b419`)
- OS: macOS arm64
- Surface: Copilot Chat
- Agent Skills enabled with `github.copilot.chat.skillTool.enabled`

No Dev Tools Console error is produced; the inline reference is simply handled as text.

Documentation:
- https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agent-customization/agent-skills
- https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/chat/copilot-chat

This is a composer UX and skill-reference parsing request, not a model tool-calling or Agent Host API request.

## Summary

Add macOS Agents Window smoke coverage through a PAC-resolved Squid proxy that requires Kerberos/Negotiate authentication, in both GitHub Actions and Azure Pipelines.

<details>
<summary>Session Context</summary>

Key decisions from the development session:

- **Reuse the existing PAC isolation harness**: The test extends the current macOS PAC/Squid smoke harness rather than reusing the Linux Docker/Apache topology from `vscode-proxy-agent`, because GitHub-hosted macOS runners already include a usable Heimdal KDC.

The smoke mock also serves ancillary endpoints over plain HTTP, so only non-CONNECT requests to the synthetic `vscode-smoke.test` host bypass authentication; the test asserts that the actual Agents Window tunnel is Kerberos-authenticated.

</details>

- Add a temporary Heimdal KDC and credential setup to the macOS proxy harness.

title: sessions: keep ignored blocked sessions ignored
body:
Ignoring a blocked session in the title bar indicator (e.g. **Ignore CI Failure**) only held until the user opened another session or the new-session view — the very same block then surfaced again, even though nothing about the session had changed.

## Root causes

Two independent bugs, both producing the same symptom.

**1. The acknowledgement state lived in a widget the command center throws away.**

`SessionsTitleBarWidget` is a command center action view item, and it created its own `BlockedSessionsIndicatorModel` — the only place acknowledged/ignored occurrences are stored. The sessions title bar calls `centerToolbar.refresh()` whenever `IsNewChatSessionContext` changes, which clears the action bar, disposes every view item and builds new ones. Opening a different session or the new-session view flips that context key → new widget → new model → every ignore forgotten.

**2. The raw blocked set briefly "unblocked" the session, which deleted the acknowledgement.**

`BlockedSessions` held its ref-counted GitHub pull request and CI model references on `reader.store`, which the observable framework disposes *before* each recompute. Since `getSessions()` returns a fresh array, every `onDidChangeSessions` recomputed the derived, dropped the last reference, disposed the shared models and re-created empty ones — so the session left the blocked set until the data was refetched. The cleanup autorun read that gap as "no longer blocked" and released the acknowledgement; when the failure reappeared, so did the pill.

## Fixes

- **Ownership** — `SessionsTitleBarContribution` now owns the `BlockedSessionsIndicatorModel` and `SessionActionFeedback` and passes them into each widget, so acknowledgements (and the transient "Approved N sessions" confirmation) survive command center rebuilds. The widget keeps no durable state.
- **Reference lifetime** — `BlockedSessions` and `BlockedSessionsCIFixModel` use `reader.delayedStore` (disposed *after* the recompute), so a recompute never drops the last reference to the shared, ref-counted GitHub models. This also removes a lot of needless model teardown and refetching.
- **Durable CI acknowledgements** — acknowledgements now record their reason. A `FailingCI` acknowledgement is keyed by the failing commit, so it is kept while the session is transiently absent from the blocked set and only expires when a *new* commit fails. `NeedsInput` acknowledgements keep the previous clear-on-absence behaviour, since their occurrence id has no per-episode identity.

## Logging

Per the ask, the feature is now diagnosable from a trace log alone:

- `[BlockedSessions] computed blocked sessions (n of m): [...]` on every recompute (level-guarded), so transient drop-outs are visible.
- `[BlockedSessionsIndicator]` traces model creation/disposal (including how many acknowledgements a dispose discards), every acknowledgement added, **kept or released with the reason**, blink queuing, and the set actually surfaced.
- `[SessionsTitleBar] creating the title bar widget` exposes command center churn.

A repro now reads as a straight line: raw set → acknowledgement decision → surfaced set.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`, `npm run valid-layers-check`, eslint and hygiene on the changed files — all clean.
- `BlockedSessions` (13) and `BlockedSessionsIndicatorModel` (22) suites pass, including two new regression tests.
- The new *"keeps the pull request and CI models referenced across recomputes"* test was confirmed to **fail** against the old `reader.store` behaviour (`blocked: []`, `released: ['owner/repo/30', 'owner/repo/30/sha30']`), so it genuinely guards the regression.

No specification update is included: `LAYOUT.md` has since been rewritten around an explicit change gate ("do not update for layout bug fixes") and no longer carries the blocked-sessions prose, so the behaviour is documented by the regression tests and code comments instead.

title: Fix lost race leaving a signed-out user on an Available marketplace
body:
## Problem

When a private/enterprise marketplace is configured (`extensions.gallery.serviceUrl`), an account change that happens **while the manifest is being fetched** can leave a signed-out (or otherwise ineligible) user looking at an `Available` marketplace.

`WorkbenchExtensionGalleryManifestService.handleMarketplaceAccountAccess` awaits the manifest fetch and then calls `update(manifest)` with no supersession. Sequence:

1. Account is eligible → a fetch starts and parks.
2. The account changes mid-fetch (e.g. sign-out) → `onDidChangeAccount` fires → `handleMarketplaceAccountAccess` runs again, sees no account, and sets `RequiresSignIn`.
3. The original, now-stale fetch resolves and calls `update(manifest)` → status flips back to `Available`.

End state: **signed-out user, `Available` marketplace.**

> Note: an earlier revision of this PR also addressed a "dropped event" defect (the account-change listener being registered *after* the initial `await`). That has since landed on `main` independently (the listener is now registered before the await), so this PR is rebased down to the remaining, still-present race.

## Fix

Add a cancellation generation so a superseded run cannot publish:

- `beginResolution()`, backed by a `MutableDisposable<CancellationTokenSource>`, cancels the previous run and returns a fresh token. It is called at the top of `handleMarketplaceAccountAccess`.
- The token is threaded into `getExtensionGalleryManifestFromServiceUrl` (replacing `CancellationToken.None`) and checked after each `await` before any `update(...)`, so a run that has been superseded by a newer account change returns without publishing.

The change is confined to `handleMarketplaceAccountAccess` and the fetch signature; no new status or behavior is introduced. Channels stay correct on their own because the constructor already re-publishes on every `onDidChangeExtensionGalleryManifest`.

## Tests

Adds one regression test to `extensionGalleryManifestService.test.ts` (GitHub default-account path): it parks the manifest fetch, fires a sign-out (`onDidChangeDefaultAccount` with no account) while it is parked, releases the fetch, and asserts the final status is `RequiresSignIn`.

Verified before/after against current `main` by reverting only the source fix (test left in place):

- **Before the fix:** the regression test fails with `actual 'available'` vs `expected 'requiresSignIn'`; the other 40 cases pass.
- **After the fix:** all 41 cases pass.

title: agentHost: stop a failed git probe from stalling Agent Merge
body:
Fixes a class of bug where a session with Agent Merge enabled sits idle forever without ever binding to its pull request, so review comments and CI failures never reach it.

Found while investigating a real session (`copilotcli:/7535d422-…`, PR #331760). Agent Merge was enabled and running — it had injected its autonomous configuration and the host was keeping the session resident for it:

```
[AgentService] Skipping idle eviction for a session held by Agent Merge: copilotcli:/7535d422-…
```

…but every evaluation died on the first check, exactly `backstopInterval` apart:

```
10:57:06 [AgentMergeController] Evaluation started: session=copilotcli:/7535d422-…
10:57:06 [AgentMergeController] Waiting for a current branch: session=copilotcli:/7535d422-…
11:07:06 [AgentMergeController] Evaluation started: session=copilotcli:/7535d422-…
11:07:06 [AgentMergeController] Waiting for a current branch: session=copilotcli:/7535d422-…
```

Its `agentMerge.controller` state had no `target`, confirming it never got far enough to bind the PR — so it never subscribed to PR events, and a review comment and a failing check both went unnoticed.

## Root cause

The session's persisted git state had lost its branch, while the worktree itself was perfectly healthy:

```jsonc
// session_metadata['agentHost.git']
{ "baseBranchName": "main" }   // no branchName, no hasGitHubRemote, no uncommittedChanges
```

`_computeSessionGitState` runs its probes independently and fills fields best-effort. `parseGitStatusV2` always yields `uncommittedChanges: 0` for any non-empty output, so its absence means `git status` itself returned `undefined`. The repository root is cached, so the function still returned an object — just a branch-less one. `_setSessionGitState` replaces persisted git state wholesale, so that object overwrote the good branch.

The failure left no trace: `_runGit` only logged when stderr was non-empty, and a timeout kill produces none.

## Why it never recovered

Three separate paths that should have repaired it did not:

1. `AgentMergeController._evaluate` calls `attachSessionGitHubPullRequest` (which begins with `refreshSessionGitState`), but only *after* the `if (!branchName) return` bail — so its own repair path was unreachable.
2. The lazy refresh on subscribe only fired when git state was entirely `undefined`; a *partial* state counted as "already computed" and masked it.
3. The file-monitor refresh needs watch interest plus an actual file change. A session held resident by Agent Merge alone — no client watching, no edits landing — gets neither.

## Changes

- **`agentHostGitService`** — return `undefined` when the status probe fails, so callers keep the state they already had instead of persisting a misleading one.
- **`agentMergeController`** — refresh git state before giving up on the branch. This also recovers sessions already stuck in this state, which matters because the bad state is persisted.
- **`agentService`** — treat a branch-less state as missing in the subscribe-time refresh.
- **`agentHostGitService`** — log git failures that produce no stderr (`warn` for timeouts/signals, `trace` for the `--quiet` probes' expected non-zero exits), so this can't fail invisibly again.

## Validation

`agentMergeController.test.ts` gains a regression test that reproduces the stall. Reverting just the controller change makes it fail the same way the real session did:

```
1) AgentMergeController
     recovers a session whose persisted git state lost its branch:
   Error: Timeout of 5000ms exceeded.
```

The git-probe change is covered by a new integration test, and was verified end to end against the compiled service: with the fix the degraded probe returns `undefined` and logs `Not reporting session git state because git status failed`; without it, it returns `{}` — the same shape as the corruption observed on disk.

Full `agentHost` unit suite: 5840 passing. The 11 failures are pre-existing and unrelated (`sessionPermissions`, `agentHostDebugLogs`, `agentHostRequestService`, `copilotAgent`, `localAgentHostMetadata`).

title: Align chat UI with design tokens
body:
Aligns the chat widget styling with the VS Code design system by replacing hardcoded visual values with semantic design tokens.

### Changes

- Uses design tokens for:
  - Font sizes and weights
  - Codicon sizes
  - Corner-radius tiers
  - Border and outline thickness
  - Spacing values
  - Theme-aware separator and shadow colors
- Applies radius tokens according to component role, including controls, inner surfaces, overlays, avatars, and pills.
- Preserves 22×22px action targets by sizing controls explicitly instead of relying on implicit `16px + 3px` padding calculations.
- Uses zero block padding and tokenized inline padding for text actions.
- Retains existing chat behavior while making sizing and visual hierarchy more consistent and maintainable.

### Validation

- Ran targeted stylelint against `chat.css`.
- Verified the diff with `git diff --check`.

title: Copilot edit tools report success even when the underlying FileSystemProvider.writeFile fails
body:
## Description

We maintain a VS Code extension that registers a custom `FileSystemProvider` for a virtual scheme. The provider forwards each save to a remote backend system in `writeFile()`. When that backend rejects the save, `writeFile()` throws a `vscode.FileSystemError` (e.g. `FileSystemError.Unavailable`), and VS Code core surfaces this correctly to the user (error notification, the editor stays dirty).

However, when a file is edited by a **Copilot edit tool** (`replace_string_in_file`, `apply_patch`, `insert_edit_into_file` → `vscode_editFile_internal`, etc.) rather than by the human, the tool reports the file as successfully **"Updated"** even though the backend save failed and nothing was persisted. **The failure is completely invisible to the agent.**

## Root cause (from reading the extension source)

The edit tools apply their changes by **streaming** text edits into the chat-editing session via `ChatResponseStream.textEdit(uri, edit)`. They never call `document.save()` / `workspace.applyEdit()` themselves, and they never inspect the result of the eventual save.

The actual save happens later, downstream in VS Code core, where our `writeFile()` throws — but that throw is entirely disconnected from the tool's result path. So the tool's *"successfully edited"* result is decided **before** (and independently of) whether the save succeeded.

The only post-edit signal the edit tool reads back is **diagnostics** (it re-reads diagnostics for the edited document and feeds new ones to the model). A `FileSystemError` thrown from `writeFile()` is not part of that channel, so it is never observed.

## Impact

Any extension whose `FileSystemProvider` can legitimately fail a save — remote/networked backends, locked resources, permission/authorization checks, quota, etc. — will have those failures **silently swallowed** when edits come from an agent. The agent believes its change landed and continues building on a state that was never persisted.

## Workaround we're using

We publish an **error diagnostic** on the file when the backend save fails (and clear it on the next successful save). Because the edit tool re-reads diagnostics, this makes the failure *observable* — but only partially:

- **Higher reasoning effort:** the agent proactively re-checks diagnostics after each edit and notices the failure.
- **Default settings:** it often does *not* re-check, and still reports the edit as fine.

So the diagnostic is a strict improvement over invisible failures, but it isn't a reliable fix — it relies on the agent *choosing* to look.

## Suggested fix

Have the edit tools observe the outcome of the save they trigger — e.g. **await the save and propagate a `FileSystemProvider.writeFile` rejection into the tool result** (report the edit as failed / not applied) instead of reporting success unconditionally. That way a failed save is surfaced **deterministically**, independent of the model's reasoning effort.

---

## Environment

- **VS Code Version:** 1.134.0 (commit `110a328ea54b42367b803ec53ee0bf52ef26b419`, x64) — stable
- **OS Version:** Windows 11, 10.0.26200.8875 (x64)
- **Feature (agent/edit/ask mode):** agent mode (edit tools: `replace_string_in_file` / `apply_patch` / `insert_edit_into_file`)
- **Selected model:** Claude Sonnet 5 and Claude Opus 4.8 (behavior differs by reasoning effort — see *Workaround* above)

title: Agents window temporarily duplicates submitted prompts in AHP-hosted sessions
body:
<!-- bug_report_template -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Not tested; reproducing it requires an AHP-hosted session in the Agents window.

- VS Code Version: 1.134.0 (commit 110a328ea54b42367b803ec53ee0bf52ef26b419, 2026-08-18T18:24:44Z)
- OS Version: macOS 26.6.2, Darwin arm64 25.6.0
- Feature: Agents window with an AHP-hosted session

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open an AHP-hosted session in the Agents window.
2. Enter a prompt and submit it.
3. While the agent turn is running, observe that the submitted prompt appears in its normal place in the conversation and also appears a second time at the bottom of the conversation.
4. Wait for the turn to finish. The second copy disappears when the turn completes.

Expected behavior:

The submitted prompt should be rendered once while the turn is running.

Actual behavior:

The Agents window temporarily renders the prompt twice. The second copy remains at the bottom while the turn is in progress, which makes it look as though the prompt was queued or submitted again. It disappears after the turn finishes.

This appears to be a UI/state issue rather than duplicate delivery to the hosted agent. It is distinct from #327586, where the same prompt was delivered to the agent twice after the first turn had completed.

body: ### Type of bug Visual regression ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open an Agents Window session that shows session metadata pills above the chat input. 2. Record a single file artifact such as `plan.md`, alongside another pill such as changed files or an issue. 3. Compare the pill heights. ### Actual behavior The single-file artifact pill is taller than its sibling pills. The resource pill measures 26px high while the shared small metadata pills measure 22px. ### Expected behavior Equivalent metadata pills in the same row should have the same height. ### Root cause The resource pill renders a themed file icon through `.monaco-icon-label::before`. Its layout box is explicitly 18px high and its image retains the default 16px size, while the rest of the row uses the compact 12px icon tier. Because the shared small button is intrinsically sized, that larger child expands only the resource button. The themed resource icon should use the same compact icon sizing token as the other icons in this dense pill row, allowing the shared button metrics to determine a consistent height.

title: [Webview] Service worker corrupts raw remoteAuthority containing - followed by four hex digits
body: Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes - VS Code Version: OpenVSCode Server 1.96.0 - OS Version: MacOS Tahoe 26.4.1 (25E253) - Browser: Safari ## Summary Webview resources return a synthetic service-worker 404 when the remote authority contains a hyphen followed by four hexadecimal characters, for example: tf-0f553fad85e991041548bd71d5f5f722073022e5.example.com The same absolute resource URL returns 200 when opened in a separate tab or when DevTools "Bypass for network" is enabled. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Serve VS Code for Web/OpenVSCode using an HTTPS hostname containing `-[0-9a-f]{4}`, such as `tf-0f55...example.com`. 2. Open Getting Started content containing images inside the VS Code webview. 3. Observe the image requests in DevTools. 4. The requests return 404 with Size shown as `(service worker)`. 5. Open the identical Request URL in a separate tab; it returns 200. 6. Enable Application → Service Workers → Bypass for network and reload; the embedded images now load. ## Root cause The webview service worker's remoteAuthority branch sends `requestUrl.host` as a raw authority. `webviewElement.ts` then unconditionally calls: decodeAuthority(entry.authority) `decodeAuthority` performs: authority.replace(/-([0-9a-f]{4})/g, ...) This assumes the authority was produced by `encodeAuthority`, but the remoteAuthority branch supplied a raw hostname. For example: tf-0f553fad... → tf3fad... → a different punycode hostname The resource lookup therefore fails and the worker synthesizes 404. The embedded request never reaches the original HTTP server. ## Expected Raw remoteAuthority values should be preserved exactly. ## Suggested fix - Distinguish encoded vscode-resource authorities from raw remoteAuthority values in the service-worker message, and only call `decodeAuthority` for authorities explicitly marked as encoded. - Alternatively, encode the raw remoteAuthority before sending it through the existing decoding path. Please add a regression test using a hostname such as `tf-0f55.example.com`. ## Workaround Avoid public hostnames containing `-[0-9a-f]{4}`. For example, `tf0f55...example.com` works. title: VS Code Chat automatically includes entire (HUGE) terminal output in model context without explicit user consent
body:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version:
- VS Code Version: 1.134.0
- OS Version: Ubuntu 26.04 (WSL 2 on Windows 11)
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): agent
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): auto
- Logs: (contains sensitive data, will not send)

## Description

When starting a chat using the built-in VS Code Chat extension, VS Code automatically includes context from the IDE, including information from open terminal sessions.

In my case, the context included the **entire output of a long-running terminal session**, including the command that was executed and all of its accumulated output. This happened without any explicit indication that the terminal contents were going to be included in the request, or an opportunity to review or exclude that content before it was sent to the model.

I only discovered this because, after several turns in one of the sessions, the automatically selected model (Sonnet) eventually failed with:

> `model_max_prompt_tokens_exceeded`

I then investigated the requests and found that the automatically generated context for the initial chat message already exceeded **500,000 input tokens**.

Importantly, this was **not isolated to a single session or model**. I observed the same behavior across multiple chat sessions under the same circumstances, regardless of which model was selected. The excessive context was already being provided by the VS Code Chat harness **before the model's first turn**; it was not generated or requested by the model itself.

The terminal in question was running a Spring Boot application in debug mode and had accumulated a very large amount of output. As a result, the automatically generated context included hundreds of thousands of tokens of terminal content.

My actual prompt was very short and specific, referring to code in a particular file. None of the terminal output was relevant to the question, yet it was nevertheless included in the model context.

This is particularly concerning from a privacy and security perspective. Terminal output can contain information that users reasonably expect to remain local, including:

* Environment/configuration information
* Internal URLs and hostnames
* Identifiers and tokens
* Application data
* Stack traces and request data
* Other sensitive information produced by development tools

I would expect context providers such as terminal sessions to either:

1. Include only a small, relevant portion of terminal output by default (for example, the most recent N lines), or
2. Require explicit user selection/consent before sending potentially large terminal contents to a model, and
3. Clearly indicate in the Chat UI what terminal content is being included in the request.

At minimum, automatically including an entire terminal buffer—especially one that can grow to hundreds of thousands of tokens—seems problematic both in terms of **privacy** and **resource/token usage**.

### Expected behavior

When terminal content is automatically added to Chat context, VS Code should limit the amount of content included and/or provide a clear indication and an opportunity for the user to review or remove it before the request is sent.

### Actual behavior

The entire accumulated output of an open terminal session was automatically included in the initial model request, resulting in more than 500k input tokens of context despite the user's prompt being unrelated to the terminal output.

The behavior was reproducible across multiple sessions and models under the same circumstances, and the excessive context was present before the model's first turn.

### Steps to Reproduce:

1. Have a terminal session with a very long ouput from the last command (or a running command)
2. Prompt anything in a new chat session
3. Observe the input tokens sent using the Agent Debug Logs feature
